structured.answer: A fixed deposit is money locked in the bank for an agreed time for interest (example 1.8% a year) minus 15% tax on the interest. What I give up is getting the money out early: breaking it needs the bank's permission and can cost a fine that wipes out the interest and even part of the money. The page doesn't say how much the fine is, so I'll ask the bank before I sign anything.

Red and a lock icon frightened me. It says the site doesn't calculate the fine, so I never learned how much breaking costs.
